Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J. 
[Crl. Misc. Amendment Application No. 01 of 2024] The case has been taken up through Video
Conferencing.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State.

Learned counsel for the applicant is pressing the amendment application stating therein that due to typographical error, the Sections 419, 468 IPC are left to be transcribed alongwith other Sections in the memo of bail application and he prays to amend/correct the same.
Learned AGA for the State has no objection to the aforesaid prayer.
Accordingly, the amendment application is allowed.
Learned counsel for the applicant is permitted amend/correct the memo of bail application, as aforesaid.

[Order on Bail Application]
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail during the trial in Case Crime No. 90 of 2024, under sections 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471,
120B of IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D of the IT Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Moradabad.
Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the instant matter due to ulterior motive.
She submits that the stolen articles are said to be recovered from the possession of the applicant but those could not be connected properly.

She next submits that the identically situated co-accused, namely, Arjun has already been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 02.09.2024 passed by this Court in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.
32252 of 2024, as such, the present applicant is also entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity.

sentences.text: She further submits that the applicant has no previous criminal history as is mentioned in paragraph no. 15 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application and he is languishing in jail since 03.06.2024 and his role is distinguishable from the role of other co-accused persons and he also undertakes that in case, he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty of the same and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.

Per contra, learned AGA appearing for the State has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that the applicant has been arrested while committing offence and stolen article articles were recovered from his possession and he has committed offence as a gang and one of the co-accused namely, Kaushendra is found well connected with the offence and the present applicant as well as the other co-accused persons were cooperating with him as such, he is not entitled for any relief.

Having heard learned counsels for the parties and after perusal of material placed on record, it transpires that prima facie no such articles are said to be recovered from the possession of the applicant so as to connect him in the instant matter and if any article or evidence is collected, so far as the Kaushendra is concerned, the role of the present applicant is distinguishable from him;
identically situated co-accused has already been granted bail; this Court has also taken note of fact that applicant has no previous criminal history as is mentioned in paragraph no. 15 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application and he is languishing in jail since 03.06.2024 and his role is distinguishable from the role of other co-accused person and he has undertaken that in case, he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty of the same and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.
Considering the submissions of learned counsels for the parties, nature of accusation and severity of punishment in case of conviction, nature of supporting evidence, prima facie satisfaction of the Court in support of the charge, reformative theory of punishment and considering larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and, without expressing any view on the merits of the case,
I find it to be a fit case of bail.
Let the applicant-Ankit involved in the aforementioned crime be released on bail, on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned,
with the following conditions:-
Ankit vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850793/
2 (1) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/
pressurizing the witnesses, or otherwise during the investigation or trial;
(2) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
He shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(3) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.; and (4) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation
, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
It is clarified that the observations made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of this bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the merits of the case.
